summary: Connect counting to how many, counting a variety of objects including pennies.
Say, without inequality symbols, whether one group of up to 10 has more, fewer or the same as another.
Compare two written numbers from 0 to 10 without using inequality symbols.
Name and describe the length, weight and height of one object with words like long/short and heavy/light.
Sort objects into categories of up to 10, count and order them; coin sorting uses only pennies.
Work with time and money: tell time to the hour and half hour, and name pennies and dimes.
Name pennies and dimes and know their values.
Count forward and back within 1,000 by 1s, 10s, 100s from any number; skip-count by 5s.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals, words, expanded form and other equivalent forms.
Solve problems with money: name coins, value coin collections, and add or subtract amounts.
Name nickels and quarters and know their values.
Find the value of a mix of quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies.
Add and subtract money within 100, dollars or cents separately, with $ and ¢ but no decimals.
Organize data in up to four categories and complete picture and bar graphs with given single-unit scales.
Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons and hexagons by sides or vertices, and name cubes, prisms, cones and cylinders.
Work with time and money: time to the minute, elapsed time, and adding or subtracting money.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes, within 90 minutes.
Add and subtract money within 1,000, dollars or cents separately, with $ and ¢ but no decimals.
Draw and describe triangles, quadrilaterals and polygons up to 8 sides by their sides and right angles.
Know metric unit sizes (km, m, cm, mm; kg, g; L, mL), convert to smaller units, and make tables.
Solve real-world problems involving money, time and metric measurement.
Add and subtract money with models and write the answer in decimal notation.
Add and subtract time intervals in hours and minutes using number lines, clocks or other models.
Add, subtract and multiply whole numbers to solve metric distance, liquid volume and mass problems.
Find the area and perimeter of rectangles efficiently, including a missing side from the area.
Show and interpret data in picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots to solve grade-level problems.
Classify flat shapes by parallel or perpendicular lines and by angles of a given size.
Use parentheses in expressions and evaluate them; formal order of operations is not required.
Solve real-world problems adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing decimals with models and strategies.
Add and subtract decimals to hundredths, including with whole numbers up to the hundreds.
Multiply whole numbers up to the hundreds by decimals to hundredths.
Divide whole numbers by decimals and decimals by whole numbers, in cases that are easy to model.
Know U.S. customary units and convert lb/oz, mi/ft, yd/ft/in, gal to fl oz and time units in multi-step problems.
Show and interpret data in picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots, including fraction or decimal measures.
Compare kinds of triangles by angles (right, acute, obtuse, equiangular) and sides (isosceles, equilateral, scalene).
Compare kinds of quadrilaterals (squares, rectangles, parallelograms, trapezoids, rhombuses) by angles, sides and parallel lines.

state_code: # SOURCES (Ohio's Learning Standards for Mathematics, adopted February 2017; ODE page last modified Feb 2026 still lists 2017 as current)

# - Cross-check of codes and lettered sub-parts: https://education.ohio.gov/getattachment/Topics/Learning-in-Ohio/Mathematics/Ohio-s-Learning-Standards-in-Mathematics/Revised-Math-Standards-in-Excel-on-5-9.xlsx.aspx?lang=en-US (labelled "2017 Math Standards Draft"; code list matched the PDF exactly)
# - Ohio keeps CCSS numbering without cluster letters; lettered sub-parts are listed as e.g. 3.MD.1a.
# - 4.G.A.3 (lines of symmetry) is not in Ohio's grade 4 (no symmetry standard in K-5).
# - K.CC.C.6 / K.CC.C.7: comparisons are oral, without inequality symbols.
# - 2.G.A.1: drawing shapes with given angles/faces dropped (identify by sides/vertices instead).
# - 4.G.A.2: "recognize right triangles as a category" dropped.
# - 4.MD.B.4 / 5.MD.B.2: fraction-unit line plots generalized to picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots.
# - 5.OA.A.1: brackets and braces dropped (parentheses only; formal order of operations not required).
# - 5.G.B.3 / 5.G.B.4: hierarchy of 2D figures replaced by describing kinds of triangles and quadrilaterals.
# - 4.MD.A.1: relative sizes limited to metric units (customary units moved to 5.MD.1).
# - Ohio's 1.NBT.2 prints the three CCSS special cases inline without letters, so it has one row.
# - Ohio adds money in K.CC.4, 1.MD.3b, 2.MD.8a-c, 3.MD.1b and 4.MD.2a; 1.MD.3b and 3.MD.1b are marked "moved" (from 2.MD.C.8) as a judgement call.
# - 5.MD.1 now lists specific U.S. customary conversions (metric moved to grade 4); kept as "edited" of 5.MD.A.1.
# - CCSS baseline: CCSS Math PDF, https://corestandards.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Math_Standards1.pdf ; ccss codes are expanded with cluster letters from the CCSS K-5 list.
# - kind is judged on content, not code: a state standard that only renames/recodes or drops/moves examples into notes is "same".
# - Lettered sub-parts get their own row (with a stem row when the stem has its own text). A sub-part that mirrors a CCSS sub-part is "same";
#   a sub-part carved out of a CCSS standard that has no such sub-part (e.g. a split of one CCSS sentence into a/b) is "edited" with a summary.
# - Sub-part rows list the parent CCSS code (CCSS sub-part letters are not used in the ccss column).
# - "moved" is used when the main content comes from another CCSS grade; the other grade's code is in ccss.
